4. Results and Interpretations
[8] At low unblocking demagnetization temperatures
(<250(cid:1)C), the specimens contain a magnetization of north
declination and steep positive inclination, which is inter-
preted as present day and viscous in origin. The polymict
breccia clasts and matrix contain a ChRM that unblocks at
highertemperatures(250–500(cid:1)C;Figure2a)withsoutheast
declinations(D)andshallowinclinations(I)(D=155.7(cid:1),I=
(cid:1)9.2(cid:1), k = 80.2 and a95 = 5.1(cid:1); n = means of 11/12 sites;
Figure 2c and Table 1). The ChRM is also identified in
alternating field demagnetization but the results were not
used in the statistical analysis because the orthogonal
projections displayed curved trajectories indicating over-
lapping components. The ChRM in the polymict breccia
corresponds to a pole position of 50.0(cid:1)N, 127.0(cid:1)E (dp =
2.6(cid:1),dm=5.1(cid:1)[semiaxesofthe95%ellipseofconfidence
around the pole]), which plots on the mid Permian part of
the APWP (Figure 3). Because all of the clasts and the
matrix have the same ChRM, the rocks were clearly
remagnetizedafterdepositionandsubsequenttotheimpact.
[9] The clasts in the monomict breccia and the host JCD
at the polymict site location contain a weak and unstable
magnetization. As a result, directional data from these sites
are not included in this paper. The JCD away from the
impact, however, contains a ChRM (D = 142.1(cid:1), I = 4.3(cid:1),

mict breccia clasts did not reveal useful inclusions, primar-

too fine grained.
5. Discussion and Conclusions
[11] Paleomagnetic data from the modified conglomerate
test results show that the polymict breccia at Decaturville
contains a post-brecciation ChRM. This ChRM is mid
Permian in age which indicates that the impact can be no
younger than the mid Permian, regardless of the origin of
the magnetization. Zimmerman and Amstutz [1972] and
Offield and Pohn [1979] report that clasts of microbanded
Mississippi Valley-type (MVT) sulfides occur in polymict
brecciasinthecenterofthestructure.Theclastshavesharp
edges indicating that they did not crystallize in the breccia,
and therefore, the brecciation occurred after the mineraliza-
tion[ZimmermanandAmstutz,1972].Estimatesfortheage
of similar mineralization in nearby MVT deposits range
fromEarlyPennsylvaniantoTriassic[SymonsandSangster,
1991; Pannalal et al., 2004; Symons et al., 2005]. This
suggeststhattheimpactstructurecouldnotbeolderthanthe
Early Pennsylvanian, and along with the pole position
obtained from the breccia, constrains the impact to the
Pennsylvanian tomidPermian (Figure3).TheJCDoutside
the impact structure contains a ChRM that is older and
unrelated to the ChRM at Decaturville.
Figure 2. Orthogonal projections (no tilt correction) of
representative specimens from the (a) polymict breccia and
(b) the JCD outside of the structure. Horizontal projec-
tions: solid points; apparent vertical projections; open
points. (c) Equal area projections showing site mean
directions from the polymict breccia in the JCD at
Decaturville (circles), the host JCD outside of the structure
(diamonds), and from the Burlington-Keokuk Formation at
the Weaubleau structure in geographic and stratigraphic
coordinates (squares) [Dulin and Elmore, 2007]. Open
symbols represent upper hemisphere projections; closed
symbols are lower hemisphere projections.
The resultsof rock magnetic studies (e.g., acquisition and
decay of an isothermal remanent magnetization) on sam-
ples from the polymict breccia and the JCD away from the
structure are consistent with magnetite as the carrier of the
remanence.
